newsitem.title: MOROCCO: Blue chips continue to drive Moroccan bourse highe.
newsitem.headline: Blue chips continue to drive Moroccan bourse highe.

text.p: The Casablanca bourse ended the week on Friday higher for the second week running, driven by interest in blue-chips, including the largest conglomerate, ONA Group, brokers said.
The all-share index closed at 437.73 points, up from 434.47 points over the previous week, a bourse official said.
"ONA and Wafabank remained the main actors on the stock exchange...They gained respectively 28 and 20 dirhams in one week," a Casablanca-based stockbroker said.
ONA group, Morocco's largest private group, was traded at 501 dirhams, up from 472 dirhams a week earlier.

ONA, showed a 20.6 percent rise in its consolidated net profit to 328.6 million dirhams in the period of January-June 1996 compared with 272.4 million dirhams in the first half of 1995. Detailed results were announced after a meeting of the conglomerate's board of directors on Thursday.
ONA and its subsidiaries control between 65 and 80 percent of Morocco's edible oil, sugar and milk market, stockbrokers said.

The conglomerate's listed subsidiaries sugar refinery Cosumar, agro-industry Centrale Laitiere, edible oil firm Lesieur and Financiere Diwan, all together posted positive results in the first half of 1996 compared with the same period last year, the group said.
Wafabank, one of the country largest banks, rose 20 dirhams to close at 520 dirhams.
Cement firm Ciments de l'Oriental, rose two dirhams 367 dirhams compared with the previous week.
Traded volume on the official market was on Friday reached 23.8 million dirhams, down from 56.1 million last week.
